question: For how many vaccine-preventable diseases are immunizations provided under the Universal Immunization Programme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) in India provides vaccinations for 12 vaccine-preventable diseases**

 
 
• Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Polio, Measles, Rubella, Severe form of childhood tuberculosis, Hepatitis B, Meningitis, Pneumonia caused by Haemophilus influenza type B
 
 
 
• **Rotavirus diarrhea**
 
 
• The UIP also provides a vaccine for Japanese encephalitis in endemic districts of selected states. All vaccines are provided free of cost. 
 
• The program primarily targets **children under the age of 5 years** and **pregnant women** to protect them from preventable diseases
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)** in India is a crucial public health initiative aimed at preventing vaccine-preventable diseases in children and women, particularly focusing on those diseases that contribute to morbidity and mortality in the country.
 
• The **UIP was launched in 1985 by the Government of India**.
 
• It **has been a key part of the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) since 2005.**
 
• The** UIP is one of the most cost-effective public health interventions and has helped reduce the rate of vaccine-preventable deaths in children under five**.
 
• Some of the program's major milestones include the elimination of polio in 2014 and maternal and neonatal tetanus in 2015
